nodes.label: SSE transport decision (D1)
nodes.rationale: The dispatcher only receives, so one-directional server-to-client SSE avoids the WebSocket and Supabase Realtime failure modes and needs no second authorisation model.

nodes.label: Thin pings, not data payloads (D2)
nodes.rationale: Events carry only resource, id, kind and timestamp; the browser re-reads through the existing authorised GET, so no GPS, photo or parcel data crosses the live channel (POPIA).

nodes.label: Org-wide channel per dispatcher (D3)
nodes.rationale: Publishing to org:{organization_id} rather than trip:{id} makes the live layer a system capability: one connection per browser, and every new screen subscribes without new plumbing.

nodes.label: Reuse auth gate, no RLS (D4)
nodes.rationale: The SSE endpoint reuses get_current_dispatcher so the backend stays the single authorisation boundary; adding Supabase Realtime would require a second, POPIA-critical RLS model.

nodes.label: Redis Pub/Sub fan-out (D5)
nodes.rationale: Events published by one uvicorn worker must reach the worker holding the dispatcher's SSE connection; in-process events cannot cross workers. Redis is already the Celery broker, so no new dependency.

nodes.label: Plain Starlette StreamingResponse (D6)
nodes.rationale: Starlette alone is enough; sse-starlette would only save heartbeat and disconnect boilerplate, and requirements.txt stays untouched.

nodes.label: Reconnect always triggers a refetch (D7)
nodes.rationale: No event replay in v1: a dropped connection may miss pings, but reconnect refetches authoritative state, so nothing is permanently lost.

nodes.label: GPS and checkpoint streaming deferred (D8)
nodes.rationale: Frequent in-transit GPS checkpoints carry real volume cost; v1 carries phase, exception and trip lifecycle signals, and GPS can be added later as an additive kind.

nodes.label: Publish after commit via per-request outbox (D9)
nodes.rationale: get_db commits after the endpoint returns, so a ping fired inside the service could make the dispatcher refetch uncommitted, stale data; a SQLAlchemy after_commit hook publishes only committed truth and nothing on rollback.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 6: Lifecycle Hardening, Integration and Demo
nodes.norm_label: publish after commit via per-request outbox (d9)

nodes.label: Fail-open publish
nodes.rationale: A Redis failure is logged and swallowed after commit, so it never breaks the driver's write; the reconnect refetch catches up regardless.

nodes.rationale: db/session.py is deliberately not edited; the drain is a registered SQLAlchemy listener in core/realtime.py so the layering direction is preserved.

nodes.label: Two incompatible auth conventions in the suite (F1)
nodes.rationale: Eleven files authenticate with the DEMO_MODE stub Bearer demo and eleven with signed make_token JWTs, and no DEMO_MODE value turns both green; decision DE1 converts the stub files during Stage 1.5 rather than quarantining them.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: two incompatible auth conventions in the suite (f1)

nodes.label: Unmocked Hedera calls in trip-creation tests (F3)

nodes.norm_label: driver pwa ci job added (lint, type-check, test)

nodes.label: What Tim's GPS work already gives P1 (analysis)

nodes.label: Frozen shared contract: phase.ts, phase-meta.ts, phase-trips mocks
nodes.rationale: Every record is keyed by PhaseType rather than a numeric union, sequence_number is a plain number, and makePhasePlan reproduces both reference plans; additive only, so existing handshake mocks survive until Stages 4 and 5.

nodes.norm_label: frozen shared contract: phase.ts, phase-meta.ts, phase-trips mocks

nodes.label: Step recipes per phase type are a draft to ratify with Tim
nodes.rationale: Loading has no driver steps under F1, seal capture moves to departure, and the old H4 and H5 steps split across unloading and confirmation; two contract questions (omit parcel_count_origin by role, ship step_recipe on the wire) remain open.

nodes.rationale: A revert of the GPS work sits in main while dev re-landed it, so the eventual dev to main promotion will conflict across the files this refactor rewrites and a wrong resolution would silently re-revert GPS work.

nodes.norm_label: main and dev divergence over gps work

nodes.label: Phase Refactor Stage 2: The Phase Engine
nodes.rationale: Makes create_trip write a full committed phase plan and replaces advance_h1 to h5 with one shared completion core behind five wrappers.
nodes.community_name: Phase Model Refactor: Parent Plan (Scope B)
nodes.norm_label: phase refactor stage 2: the phase engine

nodes.label: Shared core plus five typed wrappers (T1)
nodes.rationale: Gate, idempotency, recompute and close-if-done exist once in _gate_and_load and _finish_phase, while evidence and anchoring stay per phase because a single if/elif mega-function would be a worse abstraction.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 3: Endpoints and Schemas
nodes.norm_label: shared core plus five typed wrappers (t1)

nodes.label: Every lookup by phase_event_id, never by type (T2)
nodes.rationale: A cross-dock plan has two loading rows, so a lookup on (trip_id, phase_type) raises MultipleResultsFound; create_trip becomes the only place a PhaseEvent row is inserted.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 6: Lifecycle Hardening, Integration and Demo
nodes.norm_label: every lookup by phase_event_id, never by type (t2)

nodes.label: _is_resolved predicate: EXCEPTION counts as resolved (T3)
nodes.rationale: A phase blocks the next only while PENDING or IN_PROGRESS; exception is recorded evidence and the real hold mechanism is trip.status EXCEPTION_HOLD, checked separately, because reading the gate literally would freeze trips on every non-blocking exception.

nodes.label: Leg-scoped departure lookup for seal continuity (T4)
nodes.rationale: Fetches the departure with the greatest sequence_number below the current phase, so a destination seal is checked against the leg it actually closes and not the trip-wide first departure.
nodes.community_name: Phase Model Refactor: Parent Plan (Scope B)
nodes.norm_label: leg-scoped departure lookup for seal continuity (t4)

nodes.label: Seal fields move from loading to departure (T5)
nodes.rationale: The authoritative seal is applied at departure, and the exit guard checks the seal against the same request's value rather than a fetched prior row, which avoids a comparison of a value with itself; driver_visual_count stays on loading.
nodes.community_name: Phase Model Refactor: Parent Plan (Scope B)
nodes.norm_label: seal fields move from loading to departure (t5)

nodes.label: Legacy TripStatus values deleted (T6)
nodes.rationale: ORIGIN_GATE_IN, LOADING, ORIGIN_GATE_OUT, IN_TRANSIT, DEST_GATE_IN and UNLOADING are removed so trip.status becomes CREATED to ACTIVE to CLOSED plus CANCELLED and EXCEPTION_HOLD; the gate reads the plan, not status.

nodes.label: Stage-scoped _next_pending endpoint shim (T7)
nodes.rationale: Resolves the phase event id for the old per-type routes inside the endpoint file only, so orchestration never gains a type-based lookup and the shim is deleted when Stage 3 lands addressed routes.
nodes.community_name: Phase Model Refactor: Parent Plan (Scope B)

nodes.label: Fail-open anchor helper for departure and confirmation (task 2.5)
nodes.rationale: Catches Hedera timeout and service errors, sets anchor_status FAILED with a logged retry owed, and lets the phase complete; P0 create_trip stays fail-closed and the 504 and 502 handlers on those routes are deleted.
nodes.community_name: Phase Model Refactor: Parent Plan (Scope B)
nodes.norm_label: fail-open anchor helper for departure and confirmation (task 2.5)

nodes.label: Canonical payload functions renamed to departure and confirmation (T8)
nodes.rationale: Builder and rebuilder must change in the same commit or /verify returns db_mismatch on a healthy trip, which the dispatcher renders as tamper detected.
nodes.community_name: Phase Model Refactor: Parent Plan (Scope B)
nodes.norm_label: canonical payload functions renamed to departure and confirmation (t8)

nodes.label: Stopgap: departure auto-completes in_transit (NEW-8)
nodes.rationale: No task completed in_transit, so every trip stalled at departure; checkpoint Merkle completion is not wired, so departure auto-completes it as an authorised stopgap flagged in code.
nodes.community_name: Driver-owned arrival: in_transit becomes a submitted phase

nodes.label: Origin-count lookup breaks on multi-loading trips (NEW-9)
nodes.rationale: advance_confirmation still fetches the trip's LOADING row with scalar_one, which raises MultipleResultsFound on any trip with two or more loadings, so the 11-row walk cannot reach CLOSED; deferred and owner-less at stage close.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 3: Endpoints and Schemas
nodes.norm_label: origin-count lookup breaks on multi-loading trips (new-9)

nodes.label: create_trip must mark P0 completed (NEW-10)
nodes.rationale: A pending sequence-0 trip_creation row blocks every later phase under the sequence gate; every hand-seeded test fixture hid this, and only a chained create_trip then advance_activation test exposed it, so the regression test chains the two real calls.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 6: Lifecycle Hardening, Integration and Demo

nodes.label: Stage 2 Done When only partially met
nodes.rationale: Single-leg P0 to P6 closes with correct anchor_status, and per-leg seal continuity on the 11-row plan is proven, but the cross-dock walk cannot reach CLOSED because of NEW-9.
nodes.community_name: Phase Model Refactor: Parent Plan (Scope B)
nodes.norm_label: stage 2 done when only partially met

nodes.label: Parcel Perfect integration is read-only (evidence-only)
nodes.rationale: FreightProof records evidence and never dispatches or re-routes through Parcel Perfect, so submitCollection and requestQuote are excluded.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan

nodes.label: PP auth flow with process-lifetime token cache
nodes.rationale: getSalt then md5(password+salt) then getSecureToken; the token is cached at module level and reused without a TTL because the v28 spec says it does not expire under normal use.
nodes.norm_label: pp auth flow with process-lifetime token cache

nodes.label: PP password stored in PP_API_URL (naming conflict flagged)
nodes.rationale: The plan reads the password from the PP_API_URL setting and sends credentials and tokens as query-string parameters on a GET; the plan itself asks the team to resolve this before implementation, and it is a security-relevant open question.
nodes.norm_label: pp password stored in pp_api_url (naming conflict flagged)

nodes.label: PP_USE_MOCK canned-fixture client
nodes.rationale: A factory returns a MockParcelPerfectClient with a fixed waybill so the stack runs without real Parcel Perfect credentials, with no network calls.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan

nodes.label: getSingleWaybill response shape and parser
nodes.rationale: Details, contents and tracks arrays are parsed into dataclasses; each track trackno becomes one parcel barcode.

nodes.label: fetch_and_sync_consignment idempotent upsert
nodes.rationale: Keyed on parcel_perfect_reference per client organisation; an existing consignment is updated and not duplicated, and parcel count and raw JSON are refreshed from each response.

nodes.label: Parcel rows inserted by barcode, never deleted
nodes.rationale: The sync adds only new barcodes it has not seen, so a parcel that disappears from PP cannot erase evidence already recorded.
nodes.norm_label: parcel rows inserted by barcode, never deleted

nodes.label: Celery beat task polling active consignments
nodes.rationale: sync_active_consignments runs on PP_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS, re-fetches waybills for consignments on active trips, isolates per-consignment failures with rollback, and retries the whole task on error.
nodes.norm_label: celery beat task polling active consignments

nodes.label: Parcel scan timestamps not populated by this plan
nodes.rationale: The waybill response carries no scan timestamps in the spec summary, so pp_scan_out_at and pp_scan_in_at stay unset and the task refreshes only raw JSON and expected count; the plan says to verify against a live account first.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: parcel scan timestamps not populated by this plan

nodes.label: PP waybill sync at trip creation via pp_reference
nodes.rationale: TripCreateRequest gains an optional pp_reference, and create_trip pulls the waybill after the trip flush so trip.id is available for linking.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 6: Lifecycle Hardening, Integration and Demo
nodes.norm_label: pp waybill sync at trip creation via pp_reference

nodes.label: Poll task hard-codes legacy TripStatus values
nodes.rationale: The active-trip set enumerates per-leg statuses such as ORIGIN_GATE_IN and IN_TRANSIT, which the phase refactor later removes, so the polling filter breaks when those values go.
nodes.norm_label: poll task hard-codes legacy tripstatus values

nodes.label: respx-mocked PP client and service tests
nodes.rationale: Client tests intercept httpx with respx so no real network calls occur; service and task tests use mocked sessions and clients.
nodes.norm_label: respx-mocked pp client and service tests

nodes.label: Shared files touched by PP integration
nodes.rationale: tasks/__init__.py, requirements.txt (respx), schemas/trips.py and trip_service.py are shared and must be flagged to the team before merge.
nodes.norm_label: shared files touched by pp integration

nodes.label: Dispatcher enters only load-bearing trip data
nodes.rationale: Order number, waybill references with unit counts, crew and route are entered by hand, while cargo detail is pulled from Parcel Perfect so the dispatcher never retypes it.
nodes.norm_label: dispatcher enters only load-bearing trip data

nodes.label: TripType enum: loaded and empty_leg
nodes.rationale: Empty legs are repositioning runs with no consignments and are first-class trip types rather than a special case.
nodes.community_name: Driver-owned arrival: in_transit becomes a submitted phase

nodes.label: Versioned trip_type in the journey-lock hash
nodes.rationale: trip_type is an optional payload key included at verification only when the stored receipt carries it, because adding it unconditionally would make every pre-existing receipt recompute a different hash and report false tampering.
nodes.norm_label: versioned trip_type in the journey-lock hash

nodes.label: Zero trailers permitted in the journey-lock hash
nodes.rationale: The empty-trailer guard is removed because rigid trucks and integrated bodies legitimately run without a trailer; an empty list is a valid canonical value.
nodes.norm_label: zero trailers permitted in the journey-lock hash

nodes.label: Organization.pp_account_number resolves the client org
nodes.rationale: The PP accnum (six characters) identifies the client on each waybill, so the client organisation is derived from the waybill instead of trusting a caller-supplied id; an unknown account is a warning, not a failure.

nodes.label: TripConsignmentInput with dispatcher unit count
nodes.rationale: Parcel Perfect has no pallet grain, so the consolidated unit count (pallets) must be entered by the dispatcher and cannot be derived from the parcel tracks.

nodes.label: TripCreateRequest validation rules
nodes.rationale: A loaded trip requires at least one consignment, an empty leg may carry none, and duplicate pp_reference values are rejected; the singular pp_reference and client_organization_id fields are removed.

nodes.label: Keyed PP mock fixture library (MOCK_WAYBILLS)
nodes.rationale: Fixtures are keyed by waybill number; account MOCK01 maps to the seeded demo organisation and UNMAP9 deliberately has no organisation so the warning path is exercised.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan

nodes.label: Aspirational manifest lookup (mock-only capability)
nodes.rationale: PP v28 has no manifest-contents endpoint, so get_waybills_by_manifest exists only on the mock and the real client raises PPUnsupportedError pending a request to PP; the wizard shows the manifest field only when the capability flag is true.

nodes.label: Consignment sync resolves client org and unit count
nodes.rationale: Returns a sync result carrying the consignment and an optional warning; the idempotency key becomes pp_reference alone, since PP waybill numbers are unique within a PP instance.
nodes.norm_label: consignment sync resolves client org and unit count

nodes.label: Refresh poll must not blank the dispatcher unit count
nodes.rationale: unit_count_expected is set only when supplied, so the Celery refresh that calls without it cannot overwrite a dispatcher-entered count.
nodes.norm_label: refresh poll must not blank the dispatcher unit count

nodes.label: Trip creation syncs every waybill atomically (fail-closed)
nodes.rationale: Any PP error raises PPSyncError and rolls back the whole trip, because a trip whose cargo plan could not be pulled has no manifest, linehaul or evidence value.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 6: Lifecycle Hardening, Integration and Demo
nodes.norm_label: trip creation syncs every waybill atomically (fail-closed)

nodes.label: Empty legs carry no cargo and make no PP call
nodes.rationale: Zero consignments are created and the driver linehaul returns a defined zero consolidated unit count instead of a 404; a test proves Parcel Perfect is never called.
nodes.norm_label: empty legs carry no cargo and make no pp call

nodes.label: Dispatcher PP lookup endpoints (capabilities, waybill, manifest)
nodes.rationale: Read-only dispatcher-authenticated routes return a summary that deliberately excludes receiver contact detail and raw PP JSON.
nodes.norm_label: dispatcher pp lookup endpoints (capabilities, waybill, manifest)

nodes.label: Hedera timeout and error mapping on trip creation (504 and 502)
nodes.rationale: Journey-lock anchoring stays fail-closed, so a timeout returns 504 and a service failure returns 502 with the message that the trip was not created.
nodes.community_name: Phase Model Refactor: Parent Plan (Scope B)
nodes.norm_label: hedera timeout and error mapping on trip creation (504 and 502)

nodes.label: Dispatcher trip wizard rebuild (waybill rows, manifest fetch, empty-leg toggle)
nodes.rationale: Waybill rows validate on blur against PP, each row keeps an editable unit count, dead cargo and receiver inputs are removed, and an unknown reference yields a 422 with no trip created.
nodes.norm_label: dispatcher trip wizard rebuild (waybill rows, manifest fetch, empty-leg toggle)

nodes.label: Trip creation redesign migration (2026_07_14_ciaran_tcr)
nodes.rationale: Adds trip_type with server default loaded, organisation pp_account_number with a unique constraint, and makes consignment client organisation nullable; written by hand rather than autogenerated to avoid Supabase noise.

nodes.label: crypto/hashing.py is shared and flagged to WP7
nodes.rationale: The canonical hashing module is shared with the journey-lock workstream, so changes need to be flagged in the pull request.
nodes.norm_label: crypto/hashing.py is shared and flagged to wp7

nodes.label: Manifest service returns defined empty results for empty legs
nodes.rationale: Empty-leg trips return a zero linehaul and an empty dispatcher manifest; loaded trips with no consignments keep a 404 only for legacy data.
nodes.norm_label: manifest service returns defined empty results for empty legs

nodes.label: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: phase refactor stage 1: data model, migration, seeder

nodes.label: TripStatus coarsens additively (S1)
nodes.rationale: Deleting legacy fine-grained statuses now would silently collapse every sequence gate to a no-op and destroy the test net one stage before the engine is rebuilt, so ACTIVE is added and the LEGACY values are deleted in Stage 2.

nodes.label: Vocabulary swap is identifier-only (S2)
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 may rename identifiers but may not change any control-flow decision, sequence gate, status transition, anchor call, exception or canonical payload byte; no compatibility alias is added because a shim would hide breakage.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder

nodes.label: Canonical payload string keys frozen until Stage 2.7 (S3)
nodes.rationale: Keys such as handshake_event_id are hashed into anchored event hashes, so changing one changes every hash; re-pointing them is deferred to Stage 2.7 behind a byte-identity fence.
nodes.community_name: Phase Model Refactor: Parent Plan (Scope B)
nodes.norm_label: canonical payload string keys frozen until stage 2.7 (s3)

nodes.label: Wire key handshake_type becomes phase_type (S4)
nodes.rationale: Pydantic from_attributes forces the field rename while class names are kept until Stage 3.2, so the dispatcher reads undefined for that key until Stage 4; accepted drift.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder

nodes.label: Lifecycle reset uses ordered DELETE, not TRUNCATE CASCADE (S5)
nodes.rationale: TRUNCATE CASCADE empties whole referencing tables, so truncating trips would silently wipe every vehicle and driver receipt and the entire fleet audit trail through blockchain_receipts; ordered DELETE in one transaction keeps the scope exact.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: lifecycle reset uses ordered delete, not truncate cascade (s5)

nodes.label: A trip is immutable evidence with no deletion path
nodes.rationale: Nothing under app/ may delete a trip; the reset script is an out-of-band developer tool for the refactor database, and the RLS immutability guards for trips and phase_events were deliberately not added in Stage 1.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: a trip is immutable evidence with no deletion path

nodes.label: Reset script refuses unless DATABASE_URL names the project
nodes.rationale: dev_reset_lifecycle.py requires --project-ref and --yes and checks it against the host or pooler username of DATABASE_URL without echoing the URL, since no pg_dump backstops it.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: reset script refuses unless database_url names the project

nodes.label: Pure phase-plan generator build_phase_plan (S6)
nodes.rationale: A DB-free port of the frontend makePhasePlan rule in app/orchestration/phase_plan.py; the final stop always emits unloading and confirmation so an empty leg still closes custody. Kept out of trip_service to avoid collision with Stage 2.
nodes.community_name: Phase Model Refactor: Parent Plan (Scope B)

nodes.label: PhaseEvent model with per-stop uniqueness
nodes.rationale: Unique on trip, trip_stop and phase_type, a partial unique index allows only one trip_creation per trip, and a partial unique index on idempotency_key guards replay; relationships are deliberately not added.
nodes.community_name: Phase Model Refactor: Parent Plan (Scope B)

nodes.label: Hand-written rename migration (2026_07_28_ciaran_phase)
nodes.rationale: Renames handshake_events to phase_events rather than rebuilding it, renames constraints and the three dispatcher, driver and client-viewer RLS policies, and re-creates the trailer GPS dispatcher policy so its body names phase_events; written by hand because autogenerate would emit drop and create.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder

nodes.label: RLS gate: 3 policies, relrowsecurity true, public total 45
nodes.rationale: FastAPI bypasses RLS as service_role, so a missed policy rename produces no error anywhere; the verification queries against pg_policies are the only guard, and the policy names must follow the table.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: rls gate: 3 policies, relrowsecurity true, public total 45

nodes.label: Reference seeder on real Supabase Auth
nodes.rationale: users.id and drivers.id must equal the Supabase Auth UUID for auth.uid() to resolve and for the 0002 foreign keys to hold, so the seeder creates auth users first and uses the returned ids.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: reference seeder on real supabase auth

nodes.label: Seeded 7-row and 11-row demo trips
nodes.rationale: FP-DEMO-SINGLE-0001 and FP-DEMO-XDOCK-0001 are written directly rather than through create_trip, so seeding avoids a Hedera round trip and the seeded trips carry no journey-lock hash.

nodes.label: Eleven stub-auth test files converted to signed JWTs
nodes.rationale: Converts the Bearer demo stub to make_token with a seeded User row, which resolved the missing-user foreign key failures; fleet tests use admin_dispatcher so the require_admin_dispatcher gate does not introduce new 403s.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: eleven stub-auth test files converted to signed jwts

nodes.label: NEW-1: downgrade ordering would have made the migration one-way
nodes.rationale: The policy that names handshake_events was recreated before the table was renamed back, so downgrade failed with UndefinedTableError; the create moved to the end and upgrade, downgrade and upgrade were then proved green.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: new-1: downgrade ordering would have made the migration one-way

nodes.label: NEW-2: project-ref guard could never pass
nodes.rationale: Supabase pooler URLs carry the project ref in the username, not the shared regional host, so the guard aborted on a correct database; it was fixed to match host or username and checked in both directions.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: new-2: project-ref guard could never pass

nodes.label: NEW-7: parallel pytest runs race the shared test database
nodes.rationale: Concurrent runs against one TEST_DATABASE_URL race create_all and drop_all and produce deadlocks that look like regressions; each worker needs its own schema or the runs must be serialised.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: new-7: parallel pytest runs race the shared test database

nodes.label: Suite numbers after Stage 1 (319 passed, 8 failed)
nodes.rationale: Whole suite moved from 250 passed and 70 failed to 319 passed and 8 failed with zero skips; the remaining 8 are families scoped out of Stage 1.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: suite numbers after stage 1 (319 passed, 8 failed)

nodes.label: Phase Refactor Stage 3: Endpoints and Schemas
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 3: Endpoints and Schemas
nodes.norm_label: phase refactor stage 3: endpoints and schemas

nodes.label: Origin count is the nearest preceding LOADING, leg-scoped (S1)
nodes.rationale: Resolves NEW-9 by reading the loading row for the leg that the confirmation closes, avoiding a trip-wide lookup that raises on cross-dock trips; chosen by Ciaran on 2026-07-29 over sum-of-loadings and first-only readings.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 3: Endpoints and Schemas
nodes.norm_label: origin count is the nearest preceding loading, leg-scoped (s1)

nodes.label: Backend owns step recipes with a TypeScript drift guard (S2)
nodes.rationale: Keeps computation server-side as the stated project goal, and makes the duplicated slug list safe because a unit test parses the shared TypeScript file and fails on any disagreement; the guard was shown to bite.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 0: Test Infrastructure and Contract Freeze
nodes.norm_label: backend owns step recipes with a typescript drift guard (s2)

nodes.label: Phase read routes are driver-scoped (S3)
nodes.rationale: The dispatcher already receives the plan inside TripDetailResponse.phases, so a dual driver-or-dispatcher dependency would add a second authorisation path with no consumer.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 3: Endpoints and Schemas

nodes.label: PhaseEventRead built with from_event and a stop-sequence map (S4)
nodes.rationale: Adds trip_stop_id, anchor_status and idempotency_key plus derived stop_sequence and step_recipe; model_validate alone would silently leave stop_sequence empty, so the builder takes the stop map explicitly.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 3: Endpoints and Schemas
nodes.norm_label: phaseeventread built with from_event and a stop-sequence map (s4)

nodes.label: One discriminated complete request, not one flat model (S5)
nodes.rationale: A flat model would need phase_type to decide which fields are required, pushing honest Pydantic 422s into hand-rolled service errors; trip_creation and in_transit are deliberately absent from the union.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 3: Endpoints and Schemas
nodes.norm_label: one discriminated complete request, not one flat model (s5)

nodes.label: complete_phase is the single service entry point (S6)
nodes.rationale: Phase-type dispatch and the body-versus-row cross-check live in one function over the five existing wrappers, so the endpoint calls exactly one service function.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 3: Endpoints and Schemas
nodes.norm_label: complete_phase is the single service entry point (s6)

nodes.label: Next phase re-derived from the ledger, never trip.current_phase (S7)
nodes.rationale: The cache is only a cache; if it diverges the endpoint should expose the divergence rather than launder it, and a test corrupts the cache to prove the endpoint ignores it.
nodes.norm_label: next phase re-derived from the ledger, never trip.current_phase (s7)

nodes.label: Five handshake routes retired with no deprecation window (S8)
nodes.rationale: Neither frontend called any complete endpoint, so a deprecation shim would guard against a caller that does not exist; the Stage 2 endpoint shim is deleted outright.
nodes.community_name: Phase Model Refactor: Parent Plan (Scope B)
nodes.norm_label: five handshake routes retired with no deprecation window (s8)

nodes.label: Route spelling /phases/next instead of /next-phase
nodes.rationale: The next-phase route is mounted under the phases prefix so it stays one router; this deviates from parent section 3.2 and the Stage 5 frontend must use the same string.

nodes.label: NEW-12: ownership check must precede phase-type check
nodes.rationale: A mismatch 409 named the real phase type and returned before any driver-ownership check, letting a driver probe another driver's trip plan; complete_phase now loads the trip for the driver first, returning the same 404 as a nonexistent trip.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 3: Endpoints and Schemas
nodes.norm_label: new-12: ownership check must precede phase-type check

nodes.label: NEW-15: derived phase fields uncovered on two read paths
nodes.rationale: stop_sequence and step_recipe were tested only on the phases endpoint, though get_trip_detail and create_trip build the same schema; tests were added asserting POST and GET describe the same plan.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 3: Endpoints and Schemas
nodes.norm_label: new-15: derived phase fields uncovered on two read paths

nodes.label: NEW-17: multi-pickup then multi-drop trip reconciles the wrong consignment
nodes.rationale: On a load-load-drop-drop route the final leg has no loading of its own, so nearest-preceding reaches an unrelated pickup and raises a false WAYBILL_COUNT_MISMATCH on a correct delivery; the fix is per-consignment reconciliation using pickup and delivery stop ids, not a better sequence heuristic.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 6: Lifecycle Hardening, Integration and Demo

nodes.label: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: scan-driven loading and unloading implementation plan

nodes.label: Prerequisite: warehouse scan feed plan implemented first
nodes.rationale: Parcel scan timestamps are written by nothing until the scan feed exists, so every gate and count would read NULL and block every trip; the scan-feed plan was implemented first and this plan starts at task 3.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: prerequisite: warehouse scan feed plan implemented first

nodes.label: Stages A and B touch no frontend files
nodes.rationale: Driver app and shared contract hold Tim's uncommitted refactor, so backend semantics ship first while the driver app keeps working unchanged.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: stages a and b touch no frontend files

nodes.label: driver_visual_count made optional rather than removed
nodes.rationale: A loading queued offline under the old schema would otherwise fail validation forever and the offline queue would never drain, so the server accepts and ignores the field until no client holds one.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: driver_visual_count made optional rather than removed

nodes.label: Scan session closed signal gates the phase, not set completeness
nodes.rationale: A genuinely missing parcel never completes a set, so gating on completeness would convert a short count into an indefinite block; closing the session unblocks the phase and the shortfall is recorded as a finding, with the session key kept separate from the barcode payload.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: scan session closed signal gates the phase, not set completeness

nodes.label: Close-session dev trigger for simulating the warehouse
nodes.rationale: Scoped per stop so a cross-dock trip can close one warehouse without the other, and it drives the mock only, so the gate reads state through the same feed a real integration would implement.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: close-session dev trigger for simulating the warehouse

nodes.label: Scan counts read from live Parcel rows, never cached aggregates
nodes.rationale: Reading a cached count on the phase row to make a decision would reintroduce staleness; the only reader is a count of non-null scan stamps per consignment.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: scan counts read from live parcel rows, never cached aggregates

nodes.label: blocked_on derivation per phase type and stop (phase_gate)
nodes.rationale: Loading gates on the outbound scan session and confirmation on the inbound one, keyed per stop; three states exist, with no expected set meaning not blocked so that a trip without a Parcel Perfect reference never waits forever, and a stop with two waybills stays blocked until both close.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: blocked_on derivation per phase type and stop (phase_gate)

nodes.label: Gate served on reads and enforced on completion
nodes.rationale: The gate map is built once per request to avoid per-phase queries, a query-count test guards that, and the gate check runs after the idempotent replay short-circuit so a resent completion returns current state instead of a 409 that would stop the queue draining.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 6: Lifecycle Hardening, Integration and Demo
nodes.norm_label: gate served on reads and enforced on completion

nodes.label: Loading closes on the warehouse scan, not a driver count
nodes.rationale: The origin count is the scanned-out total, None rather than zero when no consignment exists, and the phase becomes an exception rather than blocking when the scan is short.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 3: Endpoints and Schemas
nodes.norm_label: loading closes on the warehouse scan, not a driver count

nodes.label: Scan shortfall recorded once, not twice
nodes.rationale: Scan ingest is the primary writer of the shortfall; the loading completion only adds a row when none is unresolved for that consignment and stop, since ingest's dedup compares wording and a second wording would appear as a duplicate on the dispatcher's list; a session closed with nothing scanned is the case ingest cannot see.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: scan shortfall recorded once, not twice

nodes.label: Confirmation reconciles scan-out against scan-in per consignment
nodes.rationale: Each consignment compares its origin pickup scan against its destination scan using pickup and delivery stop ids, not the preceding leg, so a cross-dock consignment is compared with the right pickup and a lost parcel becomes a scoped mismatch naming the waybill; the driver pallet count is recorded but never compared.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 6: Lifecycle Hardening, Integration and Demo
nodes.norm_label: confirmation reconciles scan-out against scan-in per consignment

nodes.label: A closed phase row is never written again (design section 2.1)
nodes.rationale: A late scan landing after unloading closed must go on a later row, because an anchored row whose fields change no longer hashes to its Hedera transaction, which is exactly the tampering signal the product detects; a test enforces that the closed row is unchanged.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 1: Data Model, Migration, Seeder
nodes.norm_label: a closed phase row is never written again (design section 2.1)

nodes.label: Shared contract adds blocked_on and the linehaul step slug
nodes.rationale: blocked_on is a string rather than a boolean so a second gate can be added without changing the wire type, and the backend and TypeScript step tables are updated together under the contract test.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: shared contract adds blocked_on and the linehaul step slug

nodes.label: Driver linehaul step replaces the blind count
nodes.rationale: The driver sees only the linehaul summary (vehicle, driver, consolidated units) with no parcel contents, shows a waiting state while blocked, and needs its document wired at the page call site because a generic render cast would otherwise leave dashes on screen without any type error.
nodes.community_name: Phase Refactor Stage 0: Test Infrastructure and Contract Freeze
nodes.norm_label: driver linehaul step replaces the blind count

nodes.label: parcel_count_origin changes meaning from declared to scanned
nodes.rationale: The same field changes from the manifest declared total to the warehouse scanned total without any type error, so every reader must be found and relabelled, including the timeline text which now says scanned rather than parcels.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: parcel_count_origin changes meaning from declared to scanned

nodes.label: Dispatcher loading, unloading and confirmation panels show scan evidence
nodes.rationale: Loading shows expected against scanned and the missing count, unloading shows the destination scan although it is stored on the confirmation row, and confirmation shows the chain of custody verdict with the pallet count explicitly marked as recorded, not reconciled.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: dispatcher loading, unloading and confirmation panels show scan evidence

nodes.label: Optional paper linehaul sheet photo (Stage D)
nodes.rationale: A nullable linehaul photo on the loading row is the only migration in the plan and is optional because a paperless warehouse has no sheet to photograph; it is third-party evidence of what the warehouse claimed was loaded.
nodes.norm_label: optional paper linehaul sheet photo (stage d)

nodes.label: Demo walkthrough with two checks no test covers
nodes.rationale: Stage two of three barcodes, close the session, confirm the linehaul shows real values, and confirm exactly one mismatch appears on the timeline; the two checks cover the cast-hidden prop and the duplicate-row guard that tests cannot reach.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: demo walkthrough with two checks no test covers

nodes.label: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: scanfeed interface and dev trigger panel implementation plan

nodes.label: Every trigger drives a mock, then the real orchestration path
nodes.rationale: A button that inserts rows proves only that the button works, whereas one that stages a mock and calls the production reconciliation proves the product; swapping the mock for a live feed then changes nothing downstream.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: every trigger drives a mock, then the real orchestration path

nodes.label: Domain facts that shape the scan design
nodes.rationale: The driver never enters the warehouse or scans, warehouse staff have no FreightProof accounts, Parcel Perfect exposes one read method only, and the scan timestamp columns were written by nothing, so origin_scan_complete was structurally false.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: domain facts that shape the scan design

nodes.label: No frontend shared or driver-app files touched
nodes.rationale: Four developers work on separate branches and Tim's driver-app refactor lives in frontend/driver-pwa and frontend/shared, so the work is confined to backend and a dispatcher-local contract.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: no frontend shared or driver-app files touched

nodes.label: Two independent switches gate the dev panel
nodes.rationale: SCAN_FEED_USE_MOCK selects the mock feed and DEV_PANEL_ENABLED registers the trigger router, which is also absent whenever the environment is production, because on an internet-reachable demo host one switch is not enough.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: two independent switches gate the dev panel

nodes.label: Redis-backed mock state store
nodes.rationale: The API and the Celery worker are separate processes, so staged state must live in Redis to be visible to both; keys are namespaced so flushing cannot touch broker keys, a connection is opened per call so no event loop is bound, and flushing uses scan rather than keys.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan

nodes.label: ScanFeed is a pull-shaped Protocol with a factory that fails loudly
nodes.rationale: Modelled on get_pp_client, the feed is polled like a real WMS would be, and the factory raises NotImplementedError when no live feed exists instead of silently mocking, so production cannot believe it has real scan data.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: scanfeed is a pull-shaped protocol with a factory that fails loudly

nodes.label: Scan reconciliation service (first writer of scan timestamps)
nodes.rationale: ingest_scans compares the expected Parcel Perfect set against the observed feed per stop and direction, stamps each matched parcel first-write-wins, and records scoped discrepancies; it is production code that a real poll would call identically.
nodes.community_name: Scan-Driven Loading and Unloading Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: scan reconciliation service (first writer of scan timestamps)

nodes.label: Discrepancy handling: warning severity, reused enum, duplicate suppression
nodes.rationale: A count difference at the door is a warning because FreightProof records rather than operates, an unexpected barcode reuses the parcel count mismatch type to avoid a cross-system enum change, an unexpected barcode is never adopted as a parcel, and identical unresolved discrepancies are not re-raised on repeat polls.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: discrepancy handling: warning severity, reused enum, duplicate suppression

nodes.label: Parcel Perfect mock override layer for mid-trip edits
nodes.rationale: Staged waybill changes are held in Redis so the Celery poll sees them, reproducing the verified portal edit that grew tracks from 2 to 27 barcodes with no version or audit field, and the override is applied only when the dev panel is enabled.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: parcel perfect mock override layer for mid-trip edits

nodes.label: PP baseline drift detection deliberately not built
nodes.rationale: The mid-trip waybill edit silently moves the expected baseline; the panel demonstrates that gap, and detecting it is a later stage, so the test asserts the silent adoption rather than a fix.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: pp baseline drift detection deliberately not built

nodes.label: Dev trigger endpoints drive the mock then the production path
nodes.rationale: Scan triggers stage the mock then call ingest_scans, PP triggers stage an override then call fetch_and_sync_consignment, exception triggers call exception_service with the trip's real driver, and mock-state flush is a POST so the shared client needs no delete verb; no endpoint writes the database directly.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: dev trigger endpoints drive the mock then the production path

nodes.label: Production absence guard and evidence-intact test
nodes.rationale: On an evidence platform a fabrication endpoint must be structurally absent in production, and flushing mock state must leave Postgres evidence exactly as it was, proving that no trigger stored anything evidence depends on.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: production absence guard and evidence-intact test

nodes.label: Dispatcher-local dev trigger page and typed client
nodes.rationale: The page is reached by URL on a second device with its own trip and stop pickers, gated by a public flag, and its types live in the dispatcher rather than the shared contract because the driver never sees parcel-grain scan data.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: dispatcher-local dev trigger page and typed client

nodes.label: origin_scan_complete becomes true through data, not code
nodes.rationale: The manifest flag was always false because nothing wrote the scan timestamps it reads, so writing them through reconciliation fixes it without editing the manifest service.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: origin_scan_complete becomes true through data, not code

nodes.label: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: precinct create, edit and anchor implementation plan

nodes.label: Precinct read and write scoping are deliberately asymmetric
nodes.rationale: Reads cover the own organisation or shared precincts while writes are own-organisation only, and a foreign write returns 404 rather than 403 so existence is never leaked; visibility is explicitly not permission.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: precinct read and write scoping are deliberately asymmetric

nodes.label: Client-supplied organisation id removed from precinct bodies
nodes.rationale: The existing create schema carried principal_organization_id as a required client field, a pre-wired cross-organisation write hole, so new body models omit it and ownership is injected from the JWT.
nodes.norm_label: client-supplied organisation id removed from precinct bodies

nodes.label: Geofence radius bounded 50 m to 5000 m
nodes.rationale: The floor matches the GPS agreement tolerance because a narrower fence would make the corroboration check fail every trip; the ceiling catches kilometres entered as metres.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: geofence radius bounded 50 m to 5000 m

nodes.label: Coordinate fields bounded before reaching Postgres
nodes.rationale: Numeric(10,7) overflows above 999 and surfaces as a 500 instead of a 422, so Pydantic enforces latitude and longitude ranges first.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: coordinate fields bounded before reaching postgres

nodes.label: Two else fallthroughs would silently break precinct anchoring
nodes.rationale: subject_visibility and verification_service both fall through to a plausible wrong answer for an unhandled subject type, returning 404 or NO_RECEIPT, so a precinct branch was added to each with failing-first tests.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: two else fallthroughs would silently break precinct anchoring

nodes.label: Precinct writes anchored to Hedera with a precinct_events ledger (D4)
nodes.rationale: Precincts were the only mutable evidence-bearing entity without a ledger, and a geofence change alters the meaning of every future handshake, so changes to coordinates, radius and sharing are anchored while renames are logged only.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: precinct writes anchored to hedera with a precinct_events ledger (d4)

nodes.label: Critical versus cosmetic precinct fields
nodes.rationale: Latitude, longitude, geofence radius and is_shared are critical and anchored, while name and address are cosmetic and logged without a receipt; is_shared is treated as critical for consistency with the vehicle is_active treatment.

nodes.label: Precinct anchor payload carries geofence in the clear
nodes.rationale: A precinct holds a business address and coordinate with no personal data, so unlike vehicle device ids nothing is hashed, which lets a later verification reproduce the geofence.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: precinct anchor payload carries geofence in the clear

nodes.label: Anchoring does not make geofence verdicts reproducible
nodes.rationale: The anchor proves that a precinct changed and when, but phase events store only a boolean geofence verdict and the journey lock covers only precinct ids, so the FP-68 verdict must also record the coordinates and radius it used.
nodes.community_name: Driver PWA UX Fixes Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: anchoring does not make geofence verdicts reproducible

nodes.label: Address geocoding deferred; click-to-place and paste-coordinates instead
nodes.rationale: A street geocoder can land hundreds of metres from a warehouse gate, comparable to the fence itself, and calling one from the browser leaks the dispatcher's address, so a point chosen on the map or pasted from a maps app is used instead.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: address geocoding deferred; click-to-place and paste-coordinates instead

nodes.label: Raw Leaflet map with satellite default and schematic fallback
nodes.rationale: Leaflet draws circles in metres natively so the fence is correct at every zoom, it was preferred to MapLibre and OpenLayers, raw Leaflet avoids a React binding dependency, and a zero-dependency SVG schematic is shown when tiles cannot load.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: raw leaflet map with satellite default and schematic fallback

nodes.label: precinct_service owns list, create, update and detail
nodes.rationale: Creates and updates append a precinct event and anchor when critical fields change, a diff that changes nothing records nothing, and the name uniqueness check is advisory because no database constraint exists yet.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: precinct_service owns list, create, update and detail

nodes.label: Event classification priority: relocation over resize over sharing
nodes.rationale: A move outranks a resize because relocating a facility invalidates more history, and the full field diff is always stored so the label is only a heading.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: event classification priority: relocation over resize over sharing

nodes.label: Precinct audit trail visible only to the owner
nodes.rationale: is_shared governs who sees the precinct in lists but never opens its change history or receipts to another organisation, so verification scopes to the owner alone.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: precinct audit trail visible only to the owner

nodes.label: Single migration adds precinct_events
nodes.rationale: The table mirrors the vehicle event ledger, is registered in the models package so autogenerate sees it, and the migration must be checked for unrelated drops before running, with a downgrade proven.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan

nodes.label: Shared precinct types and validators, mirrored bounds
nodes.rationale: The shared Precinct type gains is_shared and the mock rows are updated so the driver app still type-checks; the form validator mirrors the backend bounds as a pre-submit courtesy, and a pasted coordinate pair fills both fields.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: shared precinct types and validators, mirrored bounds

nodes.label: Dispatcher list, create, edit and detail pages
nodes.rationale: Cards suit a place, a full-page form suits a spatial task, the detail page reuses the existing event timeline so anchored and unanchored rows are visibly different, and the edit button is hidden for shared precincts the caller does not own.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: dispatcher list, create, edit and detail pages

nodes.label: Precincts in an unlabelled navigation group (D5)
nodes.rationale: A precinct is a fixed place, not fleet, and inventing a group name before a second resident exists would be guessing at taxonomy; the sidebar group key was changed to avoid a collision between unlabelled groups.
nodes.community_name: Precinct Create, Edit and Anchor Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: precincts in an unlabelled navigation group (d5)

nodes.label: Demo line: admin maps a facility and the handshake outcome changes
nodes.rationale: The story's demonstration is creating a precinct rather than editing a seeded one, because seeded precincts belong to a different organisation and the 404 rule means an admin there can see them but not edit them.
nodes.community_name: ScanFeed Interface and Dev Trigger Panel Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: demo line: admin maps a facility and the handshake outcome changes
